paragraphs: Training a machine learning model usually involves minimizing the average error across examples. Rank-based objectives offer another option: sort the individual errors and assign weights according to their positions. This makes it possible to express different performance priorities through the training objective, rather than giving every error the same contribution.

The paper develops a single optimization framework for this broad family of objectives. It covers convex examples, including spectral risk and conditional value-at-risk, as well as nonconvex examples such as human-aligned risk and ranked-range losses. Its algorithm uses a proximal alternating direction method of multipliers, bringing these different objectives into a shared optimization approach.

The authors establish convergence and a convergence rate under conditions described as mild. These are conditional guarantees, rather than a claim that every possible rank-based problem is solved without restrictions. Experiments on synthetic and real datasets also support the algorithm’s effectiveness and efficiency. Together, the results provide a common computational foundation for training with several different ways of weighting ranked errors.
neurips-2023-a-unified-framework-for-ran.tldr: A unified optimization framework handles multiple rank-based training objectives, with conditional convergence guarantees and supporting experiments.

paragraphs: Semantic segmentation assigns a category to each pixel, so its models must preserve detailed spatial information. Transferring knowledge from a larger teacher model to a smaller student can help make this task more efficient. However, existing contrastive distillation approaches rely heavily on augmented data and memory buffers, creating substantial training costs when feature maps have high resolution.

Af-DCD introduces an augmentation-free approach to transferring this dense knowledge. It combines masked feature mimicking with a contrastive objective built from partitions along both the channel and spatial dimensions of feature representations. These partitions provide a way to transfer structured local information from the teacher while maintaining training efficiency.

Experiments cover five benchmarks and several teacher–student combinations. With a DeepLabV3-Res101 teacher, the reported Cityscapes scores reach 77.03% and 76.38% mIOU for the two named student models. The authors also report improvements over independently trained counterparts across all five benchmarks. These findings support the value of adapting contrastive distillation specifically to dense prediction, where preserving local structure is central to the task.
neurips-2023-augmentation-free-dense-con.tldr: Af-DCD transfers dense local knowledge to compact segmentation models using masked features and an augmentation-free contrastive objective.

paragraphs: As semiconductor structures become smaller and more complex, atomic-scale simulation becomes an increasingly useful alternative to repeated development experiments. Machine learning force fields offer a way to support simulations at the required accuracy and scale. This paper addresses the lack of open benchmarks for assessing these models on semiconductor materials.

The benchmark includes datasets for silicon nitride and hafnium oxide, two semiconductor thin-film materials. The authors generate reference data using density functional theory under varied scenarios, requiring 2.6 thousand GPU days of computation. They also provide ten model baselines spanning descriptor-based fully connected networks and graph networks with rotation-invariant or rotation-equivariant features.

The evaluation looks beyond energy and force prediction accuracy to additional indicators of practical molecular dynamics performance. This broader assessment matters because the intended use is running simulations, so predictive accuracy is only part of the evaluation target. The contribution is a shared collection of reference data, models, and evaluation measures that researchers can use to compare approaches for these two materials.
neurips-2023-benchmark-of-machine-learni.tldr: A semiconductor force-field benchmark combines two material datasets, ten models, and evaluation measures aimed at practical simulation use.

paragraphs: Attention mechanisms decide how strongly different representations should influence one another. Transformers commonly calculate these relationships using dot products. Although effective across many tasks, this operation does not explicitly represent hierarchical relationships between data points. The paper introduces cone attention to make that structure part of the similarity calculation itself.

Cone attention uses hyperbolic entailment cones to define a hierarchy. It associates two points through the depth of their lowest common ancestor: the position in that hierarchy where their paths meet. This produces a similarity score that reflects their hierarchical relationship. The authors design the operation as a drop-in replacement for dot product attention.

Across a variety of tested models and tasks, cone attention improves task performance over dot product attention and other baselines. It also matches dot product attention’s performance with substantially fewer parameters in the reported evaluations. These results suggest that explicitly representing hierarchy can improve how attention relates data points, while also offering opportunities to reduce model size. The evidence supports this approach across the tested settings.
neurips-2023-coneheads-hierarchy-aware-a.tldr: Cone attention replaces dot-product similarity with a hierarchy-aware score and improves performance or parameter efficiency in tested settings.

paragraphs: Modern neural recording methods can track thousands of neurons, but fitting models to those recordings remains computationally demanding. Data-constrained recurrent neural networks offer a way to reproduce population dynamics and investigate the computations behind them. CORNN introduces a convex optimization training method intended to make fitting these networks substantially faster.

In simulated recordings, CORNN trains about one hundred times faster than traditional optimization approaches while maintaining or improving modeling accuracy. The authors also evaluate simulations containing thousands of cells that perform computations such as a three-bit flip-flop or a timed response. Networks with millions of parameters can be trained in under a minute on a standard computer.

The tests further show robust recovery of dynamics and underlying attractor structures despite incomplete neuron observations and mismatches in model structure or neural timescales. These findings make CORNN a promising step toward rapid reproduction of large neural systems. The demonstrated results concern simulations; real-time intervention and control in behaving animals remain motivations and possible applications rather than established outcomes here.
neurips-2023-cornn-convex-optimization-o.tldr: CORNN rapidly fits recurrent models of simulated neural activity while preserving accuracy and robustness to several observation and modeling mismatches.

paragraphs: Graph neural networks learn by passing information along edges between connected data points. Those connections can differ in difficulty, and some may introduce noise for the task being learned. Treating all edges equally can therefore produce weaker representations. This paper asks whether training should begin with easier connections and progressively include harder ones.

The proposed curriculum operates on edges rather than independent training examples. It measures an edge’s difficulty through how well that edge is expected given the model’s current training status. Training then gradually incorporates more edges in an easy-to-hard order. This adapts curriculum learning to graph dependencies, which ordinary sample-ordering strategies do not straightforwardly handle.

Experiments on nine synthetic datasets and nine real-world datasets demonstrate improved generalization and robustness of the learned representations. The findings support using the order of connection exposure as part of training, alongside the usual choice of network architecture. Because difficulty is tied to the model’s training status, the curriculum connects what the network currently understands with which relationships it should learn next.
neurips-2023-curriculum-learning-for-gra.tldr: An edge-based curriculum improves graph representations by gradually introducing connections according to their difficulty for the model.

paragraphs: A trained network’s parameters can retain enough information to reconstruct some of its training examples. Earlier work demonstrated this for multilayer perceptrons trained on binary classification. This paper broadens the investigation, asking how reconstruction extends to other model types and training objectives, and which training choices affect susceptibility.

The authors extend reconstruction to multiclass classifiers and convolutional neural networks. They also derive a more general reconstruction scheme that applies to a wider range of losses, including regression losses. These extensions show that the reconstruction phenomenon studied in earlier work reaches beyond a single architecture and a two-class prediction problem.

The study additionally examines weight decay and the number of neurons relative to the number of training samples. It observes that weight decay increases both the quantity and quality of reconstructed examples in the investigated settings. This finding makes the training procedure itself relevant to understanding what information remains recoverable from model parameters. The contribution combines broader reconstruction methods with an investigation of factors that influence their success.
neurips-2023-deconstructing-data-reconst.tldr: The paper extends training-data reconstruction to more models and losses, and observes increased reconstructability with weight decay.

paragraphs: Aligning camera images with LiDAR point clouds requires identifying corresponding image pixels and three-dimensional locations, then estimating their relative transformation. Existing approaches face two difficulties: pixels and points have very different representations, and a separate, non-differentiable pose-estimation stage prevents direct training supervision on the final transformation.

The proposed method represents the three-dimensional input using both voxels and individual points. Voxel and image branches use convolutional networks on grid-structured inputs, helping connect their representations. An additional point branch recovers information lost when points are grouped into voxels. Together, these three branches learn a shared space for matching three-dimensional elements to image pixels.

A differentiable probabilistic Perspective-n-Points solver lets the system train end to end using supervision on the predicted pose distribution. The authors also introduce an adaptively weighted loss for learning distinctive cross-modality features. Experiments on KITTI and nuScenes report significant improvements over state-of-the-art methods. The approach joins representation learning and transformation estimation so that training can directly address the alignment result.
neurips-2023-differentiable-registration.tldr: Combining voxel, point, and pixel features with differentiable pose estimation improves camera–LiDAR alignment in reported experiments.

paragraphs: Deidentification aims to make data less identifying, but the algorithms performing it can themselves exhibit privacy and bias problems. Those problems can also propagate into downstream analyses that use the resulting data. This paper describes a benchmarking effort designed to improve understanding of these technologies, with particular attention to diverse populations.

The Collaborative Research Cycle is a program from the National Institute of Standards and Technology. Its contributions combine theoretical work on equitable deidentification with public benchmark data containing diverse populations and challenging features. It also provides an open-source evaluation suite and an archive of more than 450 deidentified data samples produced by a broad range of techniques.

These resources connect questions about population diversity with concrete datasets, transformed outputs, and tools for evaluating them. Researchers can therefore investigate deidentification through a shared collection of materials instead of relying only on isolated examples. Initial evaluation results demonstrate the tools’ value for this research. The paper’s central contribution is this coordinated benchmarking foundation for studying privacy and equity together.
neurips-2023-diverse-community-data-for-.tldr: The Collaborative Research Cycle supplies diverse data, evaluation tools, and deidentified samples for studying privacy and equity in deidentification.

paragraphs: A person’s experience with machine learning can depend on several systems making decisions about them. Evaluating each model separately may miss this collective effect. The paper introduces ecosystem-level analysis, which examines the models deployed within a shared context, such as the hiring systems used by all firms receiving someone’s applications.

Across text, image, and speech settings spanning eleven datasets, the authors find a pattern of systemic failure: some users are misclassified by every available model. Improvements in individual models’ overall performance rarely reduce the prevalence of this problem in their analysis. Instead, benefits mostly reach people whom another model already classifies correctly.

The authors also examine dermatology imaging, where errors can have substantial consequences. Conventional evaluations find racial performance disparities in both models and humans, while ecosystem analysis reveals additional racial disparities in model predictions that do not appear in human predictions. The findings show why average accuracy and individual-model fairness measures can leave important collective outcomes unexamined. Considering overlapping failures provides another way to characterize societal impact.
neurips-2023-ecosystem-level-analysis-of.tldr: Studying deployed models collectively reveals shared failures and disparities that individual-model improvements can leave largely untouched.

paragraphs: Large models pretrained on unlabeled data can transfer useful capabilities to later tasks. Although this approach has transformed language modeling and has been explored for images, its applicability to remote sensing remains limited. GEO-Bench addresses the need for a focused way to evaluate progress toward foundation models for Earth monitoring.

The benchmark contains six classification tasks and six segmentation tasks. The authors curate and adapt these tasks to make them relevant to the field and suitable for model evaluation. This provides a collection spanning both category prediction and spatially detailed predictions, allowing evaluation to consider more than one kind of Earth monitoring problem.

GEO-Bench also supplies a methodology for evaluating models and combining results into an overall assessment. Results from twenty baselines establish a reference for the performance of existing approaches. The contribution is an evaluation foundation rather than a new foundation model: its tasks, reporting method, and baseline results are intended to make progress easier to assess reliably across different Earth monitoring applications.
neurips-2023-geo-bench-toward-foundation.tldr: GEO-Bench provides twelve Earth monitoring tasks, an evaluation methodology, and twenty baselines to support foundation-model research.

paragraphs: Real-time object detectors must balance detection accuracy with the time required to process images. This paper identifies information fusion as a remaining weakness in earlier YOLO models, despite existing mechanisms for combining features. Gold-YOLO targets that weakness by improving how information from multiple feature scales is brought together.

Its Gather-and-Distribute mechanism uses convolution and self-attention to strengthen multi-scale feature fusion. The authors report a favorable latency–accuracy balance across model scales. They also introduce masked-autoencoder-style pretraining into the YOLO series, allowing these detectors to benefit from unsupervised pretraining alongside the changes to feature integration.

For Gold-YOLO-N, the reported result is 39.9% average precision on COCO val2017 at 1,030 frames per second on a T4 GPU. At similar speed, this exceeds YOLOv6-3.0-N by 2.4 percentage points of average precision. That comparison supports the practical value of improved feature fusion for fast detection. The speed figure belongs to the stated model and hardware setting, while the broader contribution concerns combining feature integration with unsupervised pretraining.
neurips-2023-gold-yolo-efficient-object-.tldr: Gold-YOLO improves multi-scale feature fusion and adds unsupervised pretraining, achieving higher reported detection accuracy at comparable speed.

paragraphs: A hard-label text attack attempts to change a model’s prediction while seeing only its predicted class. It has no access to confidence scores, and text changes are discrete. The challenge is to create an adversarial example that preserves meaning, changes few words, and requires relatively few model queries.

HQA-Attack begins with a randomly initialized adversarial example and repeatedly restores original words wherever possible. This reduces the amount of altered text. It then searches synonyms for the words that remain changed, seeking improvements in semantic similarity while preserving the adversarial outcome. The process therefore balances textual fidelity with the requirement that the model still makes the targeted error.

To reduce queries, the method searches for an intermediate synonym for each changed word instead of traversing the entire synonym set. Evaluations cover five text-classification datasets, three natural-language-inference datasets, and two real-world APIs. The authors report significant improvements over strong baselines. These findings support the proposed sequence of restoring words and refining substitutions as an effective approach under the tested hard-label conditions.
neurips-2023-hqa-attack-toward-high-qual.tldr: HQA-Attack refines word substitutions to produce meaning-preserving adversarial text using only predicted labels and fewer unnecessary queries.

paragraphs: Neural radiance fields represent the appearance and shape of scenes or objects, but learning reusable knowledge across an entire category is difficult. One obstacle is the large space of possible network weights. HyP-NeRF uses a hypernetwork conditioned on a latent representation to learn category-level priors that can support several reconstruction and generation tasks.

The hypernetwork predicts both the NeRF’s weights and its multi-resolution hash encodings. Estimating these together produces significant quality gains compared with predicting only the weights, according to the authors. A further denoise-and-finetune stage cleans up rendered images and refines the representation while retaining consistency between views.

The resulting prior supports reconstruction from a single view or cluttered scenes, as well as text-to-NeRF generation. The authors provide qualitative comparisons and evaluate generalization, compression, and retrieval, reporting state-of-the-art results. The contribution combines a richer prediction target for the hypernetwork with an image-based refinement process. Together, these changes make learned category knowledge useful across multiple downstream tasks while addressing visual quality and multi-view consistency.
neurips-2023-hyp-nerf-learning-improved-.tldr: HyP-NeRF learns reusable category-level NeRF priors by predicting weights and hash encodings, then refining rendered quality while preserving view consistency.

paragraphs: Semantic segmentation benefits from context: relationships between different image regions can help determine each pixel’s label. Existing context mechanisms often rely on predetermined assumptions about scale or similarity, which can produce inadequate information aggregation. IDRNet instead uses deletion diagnostics to guide how contextual relationships are modeled.

The method first groups pixel representations into semantic-level representations using pseudo labels. A feature enhancement module makes these groups more distinguishable. It then examines network outputs through a deletion-based diagnostic procedure to infer relationships among the grouped representations. Those relationships guide how the groups exchange information, and the updated group representations enrich the original pixel features before final prediction.

This design makes the network’s response to interventions part of determining which contextual information should interact. Quantitative and qualitative experiments support the method’s effectiveness. The authors report consistent improvements when adding the context scheme to state-of-the-art segmentation frameworks, along with competitive results on ADE20K, COCO-Stuff, PASCAL-Context, LIP, and Cityscapes. The findings support intervention-guided context modeling as a useful addition to established segmentation systems.
neurips-2023-idrnet-intervention-driven-.tldr: IDRNet uses deletion diagnostics to learn contextual relationships that improve pixel-level semantic segmentation.

paragraphs: Human demonstrations can contain several different ways of performing a task. In imitation learning, a policy trained with a maximum-likelihood objective may average these distinct behaviors, potentially producing actions that are ineffective or unsafe. Information Maximizing Curriculum addresses this problem by changing how individual demonstrations contribute to learning.

The method assigns a weight to each data point and encourages a model to specialize in behavior it can represent. It can therefore ignore examples from modes it cannot capture, reducing pressure to average incompatible behaviors. To recover versatility across the dataset, the authors extend this approach to a mixture of experts, with each component selecting its own training subset.

A maximum-entropy-based objective is introduced to encourage full dataset coverage across the mixture. Specialization and coverage thus play complementary roles: individual experts focus, while the overall policy is designed to encompass the different behavior modes. Experiments on complex simulated control tasks with varied human demonstrations report superior performance over state-of-the-art methods, supporting this curriculum-based approach to learning versatile policies.
neurips-2023-information-maximizing-curr.tldr: Information Maximizing Curriculum combines selective learning and a mixture of experts to reduce behavior averaging in imitation learning.

paragraphs: Program synthesis searches for programs that perform a desired computation. Neural models can guide that search using information from candidate executions, but several earlier approaches cannot handle loops, higher-order functions, or lambda functions. Those restrictions limit the kinds of longer and more general programs they can construct.

LambdaBeam introduces a search algorithm that builds arbitrary lambda functions by composing operations available in a given domain-specific language. It represents the execution behavior of these functions as semantic vectors. A neural policy then uses these representations to choose which lambdas to construct during the search, connecting the search decisions to what candidate functions actually do.

The constructed lambdas can be passed to higher-order functions to carry out looping computations. This extends neural program search beyond candidates that lack these functional building blocks. In an integer-list-manipulation domain, LambdaBeam outperforms the tested neural, symbolic, and language-model-based techniques. The results support its approach within that domain, while the construction capability remains defined by the operations available in the chosen language.
neurips-2023-lambdabeam-neural-program-s.tldr: LambdaBeam guides program search with execution-based representations of lambda functions, enabling higher-order looping computations.

paragraphs: Machine unlearning seeks to remove particular training examples’ influence from a model. Retraining on the remaining data provides an exact route, but its computational cost motivates approximate methods. This paper studies how changing the model itself, through weight pruning, can bring approximate unlearning closer to that retraining reference.

The authors show theoretically and empirically that sparsity can improve unlearning across multiple criteria while preserving efficiency. This motivates a procedure that prunes the model before applying an unlearning method. They also develop a sparsity-aware approach that uses regularization during approximate unlearning, making sparsity part of the unlearning training process.

Experiments report consistent benefits across several unlearning scenarios. One highlighted result is a 77% gain in unlearning efficacy for fine-tuning when using the proposed sparsity-aware method. The paper also demonstrates applications to backdoor defense and transfer learning through removal of a source class. These results position model sparsity as a useful factor in unlearning performance, with applications extending beyond the removal of data for privacy purposes.
neurips-2023-model-sparsity-can-simplify.tldr: Pruning and sparsity-aware training can improve approximate machine unlearning and reduce its gap from full retraining.

paragraphs: Online news increasingly includes firsthand, unedited recordings alongside professionally produced broadcasts. Existing news-video datasets mainly emphasize traditional broadcasts for English-speaking audiences, leaving much of this variety underrepresented. MultiVENT expands the available research data to include multiple languages and different forms of event coverage.

The dataset centers on events and connects videos with text documents across five target languages. It includes both broadcast news and non-professional footage. This combination gives researchers material for studying how different presentation formats and languages describe events, rather than restricting evaluation to a single style of news production.

The authors use MultiVENT to analyze online news videos and consider how such material could support robust, factually accurate models. They also provide a baseline model for complex multilingual video retrieval. This establishes an initial approach for finding relevant videos using the dataset. The contribution is a broader dataset and retrieval starting point; improved factual accuracy is a motivation for using these resources, rather than a demonstrated property of every model trained on them.
neurips-2023-multivent-multilingual-vide.tldr: MultiVENT connects multilingual event videos with text across five languages and supplies a baseline for complex video retrieval.

paragraphs: Generating several views of the same scene requires the images to agree where their contents overlap. MVDiffusion addresses this task using text prompts and supplied pixel-to-pixel correspondences. These correspondences can come from perspective crops of a panorama or from depth maps and camera poses for multiple views.

The method generates the views simultaneously with a pretrained text-to-image diffusion model. Correspondence-aware attention layers allow information to pass between views during generation. This gives each view access to the others and addresses error accumulation associated with repeatedly warping and filling in images in sequence.

For panorama generation, the model is trained on ten thousand panoramas and produces high-resolution photorealistic outputs from text. It can also extend one perspective image into a full 360-degree view. For multi-view generation conditioned on depth, the authors report state-of-the-art scene-mesh texturing performance. These findings support coordinated generation as a way to improve consistency across views, with the supplied correspondences providing the structural links between the images.
neurips-2023-mvdiffusion-enabling-holist.tldr: MVDiffusion generates views jointly using supplied pixel correspondences and cross-view attention to improve consistency.

paragraphs: A model can encounter new data that differs from its training data in several distinct ways. Input frequencies may change, or the relationship between inputs and outcomes may change. This paper argues that identifying the kind of shift matters because different shifts call for different algorithmic and operational responses.

The authors examine natural shifts in five tabular datasets across more than 86,000 model configurations. They find that changes in the outcome distribution conditional on inputs, written Y|X, are the most prevalent in this investigation. This matters because conclusions drawn under covariate shifts can fail when the input–outcome relationship itself changes.

The paper introduces WhyShift, a testbed of curated real-world shifts whose types are explicitly characterized. It also identifies regions of the input space experiencing the largest Y|X changes and discusses implications for algorithmic and data interventions. The contribution links performance evaluation with a more precise description of what changed. Its findings encourage research into why datasets differ, so that benchmark conclusions and proposed remedies address the relevant shift.
neurips-2023-on-the-need-for-a-language-.tldr: WhyShift characterizes real-world tabular shifts and shows why changes in input–outcome relationships deserve explicit attention.

paragraphs: Distributed estimation combines information from separate participants to infer unknown parameters. Communication limits, local privacy requirements, or restrictions on measurements can constrain what each participant reveals. This paper studies the best achievable estimation accuracy under such constraints, including protocols in which participants interact.

The authors develop a unified framework for proving minimax lower bounds: limits on how small the worst-case estimation error can be. The framework applies to different continuous and discrete distribution families and to any ℓp loss. Its reusable structure makes it possible to derive bounds across a broad range of estimation problems while accounting for local information restrictions.

For Gaussian distributions, the approach avoids limitations of earlier techniques. It also recovers bounds previously obtained through data-processing inequalities and Cramér–Rao methods. For the families considered, the authors provide matching upper bounds, establishing that the lower limits can be attained at the corresponding level of accuracy. This pairing distinguishes a fundamental information constraint from a shortcoming of a particular estimator and clarifies what interactive procedures can achieve.
neurips-2023-unified-lower-bounds-for-in.tldr: A unified framework establishes achievable accuracy limits for interactive distributed estimation under communication, privacy, and measurement constraints.

paragraphs: Camera images and LiDAR point clouds provide complementary information for three-dimensional object detection. However, existing combined detectors do not fully use image information to address weaknesses of LiDAR-based detection. UPIDet develops two ways for the image branch to contribute more strongly, particularly when the point cloud is sparse.

First, it adds a two-dimensional auxiliary task called normalized local coordinate map estimation. This encourages image features to encode local spatial information that can supplement the point cloud. Second, a point-to-pixel module allows training objectives from the image branch to send gradients into the point-cloud backbone, improving its learned representations.

These mechanisms give images a role both in providing spatial features and in shaping how point-cloud features are learned. Experiments and ablation studies support the effectiveness of the approach. The authors report the top position in the cyclist category of KITTI at submission time. That result is specific to the stated category and timing, while the broader finding is that image-branch supervision can strengthen a combined three-dimensional detector.
neurips-2023-unleash-the-potential-of-im.tldr: UPIDet strengthens 3D detection by learning spatial image features and using image-training gradients to improve point-cloud representations.

paragraphs: Recorded behavior often comes without rewards specifying which actions are desirable. Such data still contains useful knowledge, but offline reinforcement learning does not fully exploit it. UBER proposes extracting a collection of behaviors from reward-free datasets before using those behaviors to help learn new tasks.

The approach assigns different agents different artificial rewards sampled from a prior distribution. Each reward encourages the extraction of a different behavior from the same offline data, producing candidate policies for later reuse. The authors show that rewards generated by random neural networks are sufficient to recover diverse, useful behaviors, including some close to expert behavior.

The paper provides both theoretical and empirical evidence for using these random reward priors. Across multiple benchmarks, the resulting behavior collections improve sample efficiency in online reinforcement learning and outperform existing baselines. The significance is that useful behavioral starting points can be obtained without manually specifying rewards for the original dataset. This reduces reliance on human supervision while allowing later task learning to benefit from previously recorded behavior.
neurips-2023-unsupervised-behavior-extra.tldr: UBER uses random artificial rewards to extract diverse policies from reward-free data and improve subsequent reinforcement learning.

paragraphs: No-reference video quality assessment models estimate visual quality without requiring a reference video. Strong prediction performance alone does not establish how these models respond to deliberately crafted input changes. This paper investigates their adversarial robustness and introduces a patch-based random-search method for attacks without access to the model’s internal workings.

The attack objective is to move the predicted quality score away from the ground-truth score while keeping the video’s appearance within a just-noticeable-difference constraint. A proposed Score-Reversed Boundary Loss pushes the estimate toward a selected boundary. The perceptual constraint is represented using strict restrictions on both L2 and L∞ perturbation norms.

This formulation connects the attack’s effect on the numerical score with limits on visible changes to the video. The authors report that it supports effective, imperceptible attacks in both white-box and black-box settings. The contribution exposes a reliability concern for quality assessment: a model’s estimated score can be manipulated while the permitted visual perturbation remains small. It also supplies a concrete framework for testing that vulnerability.
neurips-2023-vulnerabilities-in-video-qu.tldr: The paper probes video-quality models with attacks that distort predicted scores while constraining perceptible changes to the video.
